claims.text: Schwab and Raymond James each describe a value proposition to independent advisors built on a full platform of capabilities and support, though each leads with a different emphasis.

Schwab states it built its advisor business around helping independent advisors grow, compete and succeed, offering a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.

Schwab describes this as the leading RIA support ecosystem and a differentiated, full-service platform built on scale and reputation, breadth beyond custody, operational excellence, and dedicated service and support.

Raymond James frames its independent contractor offering as a partnership in independence, letting advisors run their own practice while accessing the firm's full capabilities at a level right for their business.

CEO Paul Shoukry describes a best-of-both-worlds value proposition, a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, with a strong balance sheet and commitment to independence as a differentiator.

A side-by-side comparison is valid: both firms describe their value proposition in their own words on overlapping terms, with Schwab leading on scale and breadth beyond custody (custody, trading, banking, lending, technology, and service) and Raymond James leading on advisor- and client-focused culture, commitment to independence, and choice across affiliation options.
